subject: EdgeAI Labs: dedicated capacity ask & runway
messages:
From: Tom Keller <tom.keller@edgeailabs.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Pilot capacity ask — short runway

Hi Rafael,

We're excited to kick off the pilot next month. Quick ask — our product team expects a burst of traffic for a two-week evaluation (expected close 12/10) and wants a dedicated pool to guarantee latency SLAs.

High-level numbers: estimated peak concurrency ~45 concurrent sessions, avg seq length ~1k tokens, expected total tokens/day ~75M during the burst window. We attached a small workbook with per-environment forecasts.

Can Redwood provide a recommended reserve (GPU count / expected throughput) and an estimate of monthly committed cost? We need to confirm internally by EOD 11/30.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Keller | Head of Platform
EdgeAI Labs
Attachment: EdgeAI_capacity_request.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Tom Keller <tom.keller@edgeailabs.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot capacity ask — short runway

Tom — thanks for the forecast and for sharing the workbook. Looping in Jordan (SE) to ground-truth the workload profile and Keith/infra (cc'd separately) for pool availability.

Quick ask for us to size conservatively: can you confirm
- expected QPS per client (or concurrent session definition)
- whether the 75M tokens/day is sustained or concentrated in a 6–8 hour window
- any strict region constraints (we can offer lower-cost eu/apac options but that changes latency)

I'll pull an initial reserve suggestion once Jordan confirms the model variant and burst shape.

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes | Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Tom Keller <tom.keller@edgeailabs.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T09:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot capacity ask — short runway

Tom — reviewed the workbook. A couple of clarifying notes (copying the most relevant excerpts):

On Tue, Nov 24, 2026 at 09:12 Tom Keller <tom.keller@edgeailabs.com> wrote:
> High-level numbers: estimated peak concurrency ~45 concurrent sessions, avg seq length ~1k tokens, expected total tokens/day ~75M during the burst window.

If those concurrency numbers represent simultaneous interactive sessions, recommend we size for 60 concurrent to give headroom for spikes and KV cache warm-up.
Model variant: from your prompt profile it looks like an Llama2-13B-like model in fp16. For latency SLO ~150–200ms/token we estimate ~8 RTX-6000-equivalent GPUs for steady-state at that concurrency with continuous batching; for burst windows (6–8h concentrated) we should provision 12 GPUs to keep tail latency under SLO.

If you prefer a lower-commit option, we can mix dedicated reserve (8 GPUs) + burst slots (up to 8 additional on pay-as-you-go). That reduces committed monthly cost but introduces burst availability risk.

Kimberly — can you confirm how finance views an 8 vs 12 GPU monthly committed ask for a pilot (cost/approval fast-track)? Ben — are those 8/12 values reasonable given current pool and burst capacity?

—Jordan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-26T14:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot capacity ask — short runway

Quick finance view: we can approve a one-month committed reservation for a pilot if revenue is expected and legal signs a short MSA addendum. Costbacks: an 8-GPU commit (NVIDIA A100-equivalent pricing) looks like ~$40k/month list; 12 GPUs ~ $57k/month list.

If Rafael needs approval faster than procurement (ACME internal timelines), finance can provision a short-term credit to cover the pilot with the understanding the customer signs by 12/15 or we convert to a short-term contract.

Request: Rafael, please confirm the recommended configuration (8 commit vs 8 + burst vs 12 commit) and I will prepare the approval memo. Also attaching a Q4 availability snapshot (internal) for infra to reference.

Attachment: q4_gpu_availability_snapshot.csv
—Kimberly
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T10:17:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot capacity ask — short runway

Short infra note: current US west pool has limited burst slots for the 12/6–12/20 window due to overlapping Reserved commitments. However, we can offer
- 8 dedicated GPUs in us-west available immediately
- up to 6 burst GPUs across us-east and eu-west if cross-region routing is acceptable (we can add a region-aware policy to keep latency within SLO for a subset of clients)

Operational caveat: cross-region burst increases complexity for customer IP allowlists and data residency. If the customer requires all traffic in us-west, we recommend 12-commit GPUs.

I'll mark tentative capacity in the pool for 48 hours pending deal approval.
—Ben
Infrastructure Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Tom Keller <tom.keller@edgeailabs.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot capacity ask — short runway — mutual action plan

Tom — thanks for the quick turnaround. Proposal and next steps below:

Summary recommendation (based on Jordan/Ben):
- Option A (lowest risk): 12-GPU committed in us-west for the 12/6–12/20 pilot window. Estimated list cost: $57k/month.
- Option B (cost-efficient): 8-GPU committed in us-west + up to 6 burst GPUs (us-east / eu-west) to cover spikes. Estimated committed cost: $40k/month + burst usage.

Requested from EdgeAI Labs by 11/30 EOD: please confirm preferred option and sign the attached short MSA addendum. If you need finance to short-term sponsor (Kimberly offered), state so in reply and we will provision conditional credit to hold capacity.

Action items (owners):
- Tom: reply with Option A or B, and confirm region constraints (due 11/30 EOD)
- Rafael: prepare initial contracting/short addendum and send to customer (ETA 11/30 17:30 PST)
- Kimberly: prepare approval memo and conditional credit terms if requested (ETA 11/30 18:00 PST)
- Ben: hold tentative 8 GPUs and hold additional 4 GPUs for 48 hours (confirmed)

If we don't get a firm choice by EOD, Ben will release the tentative holds and we will revert to the pay-as-you-go fallback which may add burst availability risk. Follow-up call scheduled if needed on 12/01 — 10am PST.

Thanks team — Rafael
Rafael Mendes | Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
